q: Why might anaesthesia be lightened during trigeminal ablation?
o: So the patient can respond during sensory testing
why: Some surgeons test the needle position with the patient responding before lesioning.

q: Which drug is first line for trigeminal neuralgia?
why: Carbamazepine; check sodium as it can cause hyponatraemia.

q: What can happen with needle placement through the foramen ovale?
why: Trigeminal stimulation can cause sudden bradycardia; atropine should be ready.

q: What advice is given if the cornea is numb after ablation?
why: A numb cornea can be damaged without the patient noticing.

q: Why induce on the table before rotating it?
o: The airway is distant once the table is turned
why: Secure the airway before the head end moves away from you.
